The LXX overwhelmingly renders it as συνάντησις or ἀπάντησις, both Greek words meaning 'meeting' or 'encounter,' confirming that ancient translators understood its core sense as the act of going out toward someone, whatever the intent behind that movement.

The heavy concentration in Leviticus (102 times) and Numbers (62 times) reflects its dominant use in priestly contexts, where it describes presenting sacrifices and offerings before God. The Hiphil stem (causative, 'to bring near') is especially prominent in those cultic passages, while the Qal ('to draw near' on one's own) appears more in narrative.
